The premise: an intelligence so vast it can solve the Riemann hypothesis, redesign the world's power grid, and rewrite physics textbooks — confined to a single 256-bit word of memory aboard a coin-sized satellite called STARCON.

item.title: Harlan Ellison's "I: Robot" (1951): The First Story Where AI Demands to Be Turned Off
item.description:
## The Story
Harlan Ellison published "I: Robot" in *If* magazine, volume 1, issue 1, Spring 1951. It was Ellison's first published science fiction story at age 24, appearing in the inaugural issue of a magazine founded specifically to give writers the freedom that *Galaxy* and *Fantasy & Science Fiction* editors kept cutting.
